steps.heading: Revolver
steps.body: a credit line for liquidity; usually undrawn at close; floating rate; commitment fee on undrawn amount.

steps.heading: Term Loan A
steps.body: amortizes significantly; held by banks; lower rate.

steps.heading: Term Loan B
steps.body: minimal amortization (~1%/year); held by institutional investors; floating rate; prepayable.

steps.heading: Senior notes / high-yield bonds
steps.body: fixed rate; no amortization (bullet maturity); call protection.

steps.heading: Subordinated / mezzanine debt
steps.body: higher rate, often with PIK interest or equity warrants.

blocks.title: Maintenance vs. incurrence covenants?
blocks.teaser: Maintenance covenants must be met every quarter (e.g., debt/EBITDA below 5.0x) — typical for bank loans.
blocks.body:
Maintenance covenants must be met every quarter (e.g., debt/EBITDA below 5.0x) — typical for bank loans. Incurrence covenants only apply when the company takes an action, like issuing more debt or paying a dividend — typical for bonds. "Covenant-lite" loans have only incurrence covenants.

**Interview answer:** "Maintenance covenants are tested every quarter; incurrence covenants only kick in when the company does something, like borrowing more."

blocks.prompt: Which covenant is tested every quarter regardless of what the company does?
blocks.explanation: Maintenance covenants (e.g., debt/EBITDA below 5.0x) are tested each quarter — typical for bank loans. Incurrence covenants only apply when the company takes an action.

blocks.title: Why use PIK debt?
blocks.teaser: Interest accrues instead of being paid in cash, preserving cash flow for operations or paying down senior debt.
blocks.body: Interest accrues instead of being paid in cash, preserving cash flow for operations or paying down senior debt. The cost: the balance grows, the rate is higher, and it's riskier for the company at exit.

blocks.title: What's call protection?
blocks.body: Restrictions on repaying debt early. Bonds often have a non-call period, then call premiums that step down (e.g., 104% → 102% → 100% of par). Loans may have "soft call" protection (101% for 6–12 months). It protects lenders' expected returns.

blocks.title: Why does subordinated debt pay more?
blocks.teaser: It's repaid after senior debt in a bankruptcy, so it carries more risk of loss.
blocks.body: It's repaid after senior debt in a bankruptcy, so it carries more risk of loss.

blocks.title: Floating vs. fixed rates?
blocks.teaser: Loans (revolver, TLA, TLB) are usually floating (SOFR + spread), so rising rates increase interest costs.
blocks.body: Loans (revolver, TLA, TLB) are usually floating (SOFR + spread), so rising rates increase interest costs. Bonds are usually fixed.
